contracts.name: Accordion
contracts.layerWhy: It discloses detail; reading it is not a job.
contracts.promise: Each summary opens the detail under it, without moving what I'm reading.
contracts.expectation: Summaries one under the other with a chevron that turns.
contracts.evidence: Native <details>: it works without script, is found by the browser's search, and same-named ones open one at a time.
behaviour: Enter or Space on a summary toggles it.
contracts.context: Answers people skim, settings people rarely open.
relationships: Same name, one open.
accessibility: Native details and summary semantics.
failures: Never hides something everyone needs.
dont: An accordion around a whole page.

contracts.name: Alert
contracts.layerWhy: It says one fact about the place it sits in; acting on the fact is up to the page.
contracts.promise: Something about this place is true, and stays true until it changes.
contracts.expectation: A message above what it is about that won't go away until the situation does.
contracts.evidence: Its tone is a mark and words as well as colour; it has no close button; a banner variant speaks for the whole product.
behaviour: Stays until the condition changes.
With [live], appearing after load, it is announced (danger urgently).
contracts.context: Above the page, section or form it is about. Not for the result of an action just taken.
relationships: Its place is "alert" (or "banner") in the behaviour model.
Its actions sit inside it, under the words.
accessibility: role="status" or role="alert" only when it appears after load.
The mark is drawn by CSS, the words carry the meaning.
failures: Never dismissible: a fact is changed, not hidden.
Never colour alone.
do: Title the fact; say what to do in the body.
dont: An alert for "Saved".
Several alerts stacked about one thing.

contracts.name: Autocomplete
contracts.layerWhy: One field with suggested answers; still one question.
contracts.promise: Typing narrows a list of answers; with [strict], only one of them is a valid answer.
contracts.expectation: A text field that opens a list on focus or click, marking what matches the words typed.
contracts.evidence: Matches are marked, a status says how many, an empty result says so; a search box opens on focus with its own blank list.
behaviour: Opens on click, ↓, or on focus with [openOnFocus].
[blank] options show while the field is empty.
Text that differs only by case or accents becomes the option on leaving.
contracts.context: Cities, people, pages: a long list someone partly knows. Search boxes.
relationships: Typing narrows; the chosen answer is the field's value.
accessibility: combobox with aria-autocomplete="list"; the count is announced.
failures: Never blank while it has something to offer.
do: Give a search box a blank list.
dont: Strict on a field where any answer is valid.

contracts.name: Avatar
contracts.layerWhy: It stands for a person or one thing; no job.
contracts.promise: This is who or what it is.
contracts.expectation: A round picture or initials.
contracts.evidence: Its name is what is read; initials stand in when the picture is missing or fails.
behaviour: Overlapping avatars form a group.
contracts.context: Beside a name, in a list, in a bar.
relationships: It goes with the person's name nearby.
accessibility: role="img" with the name; the initials are hidden from reading.
failures: Never the only place a name appears.
dont: An avatar for a non-person object with a person's look.

contracts.name: Badge
contracts.layerWhy: It states one short fact about something; no job.
contracts.promise: This thing has this fact: New, 3, Overdue.
contracts.expectation: A small pill on or beside the thing.
contracts.evidence: Always words or a number, so it reads without colour; the tone only adds.
behaviour: A number is lined up as tabular digits.
contracts.context: Counts and short states.
relationships: It belongs to the thing it sits on.
accessibility: An aria-label when a number needs words ("12 unread").
failures: Never colour alone.
Never decoration.
dont: A badge and a status saying the same thing.

contracts.name: Breadcrumbs
contracts.layerWhy: It goes up a hierarchy; moving is not a job.
contracts.promise: Each step is a real level above this one, and the last is where you are.
contracts.expectation: Links separated by slashes, ending in the current place in plain words.
contracts.evidence: The current place is not a link and is marked aria-current.
behaviour: Wraps on narrow widths.
contracts.context: Places inside a real hierarchy. Not a history of where the person has been.
relationships: Each step names a place.
accessibility: A <nav> labelled "Breadcrumb" with an ordered list.
failures: Never invents a level that isn't a place.
dont: Breadcrumbs on a flat site.

contracts.name: Button
contracts.layerWhy: It keeps one part of a promise: this action happens when pressed. It does no whole job alone, however interactive it is.
contracts.promise: Pressing it does the one thing its words say, once.
contracts.expectation: Pressing it starts something now, and it will say what happened.
contracts.evidence: It goes busy within 100 ms, ignores a second press while busy, and says its outcome where it is ("Saved") and aloud.
behaviour: Activates on pointer, touch, Enter and Space.
With [run], busy at once and for at least 450 ms, then shows the returned word for two seconds.
A second press while busy, or any press while aria-disabled, is stopped before any (click) on it runs.
A destructive kind always wears the danger edge; its final step the danger fill.
contracts.context: Where a person can expect an action: the end of a form, a row of actions, inside an item. Never to move between places; that is a link.
relationships: Its label is the person's verb and an object: "Save Changes".
Emphasis ranks it among its siblings: one primary per place.
A destructive one sits apart from safe ones (.pr-actions).
accessibility: A native <button>, so it is announced and pressed as one.
Its outcome is announced through a polite live region.
aria-busy while working; aria-disabled keeps it in the tab order to explain why.
The focus ring is always visible from the keyboard.
failures: Never ignores a press without showing it was heard.
Never says it is done before the work is.
Never runs twice for one intention.
Never reads "Submit", "OK" or "Click here".
do: Name the action and its object.
Use aria-disabled with a reason in the description rather than disabled.
dont: Two primary buttons in one place.
A Delete beside Save at the same weight.
A button that only navigates.

inputs: kind: the action kind (mutative by default)
final: the last step of an irreversible action
run: the work; its returned word is said in place

contracts.name: Button group
contracts.layerWhy: It joins a few buttons that act on one thing; it is still a single control, not a job.
contracts.promise: Its buttons act on the same thing, and with aria-pressed only one or some are on.
contracts.expectation: The buttons sit joined, under one name, so they read as one control.
contracts.evidence: The pressed button sits in the primary's quiet fill and is announced as pressed; the group has one name.
behaviour: Buttons are joined with shared outer corners.
With aria-pressed, each is a toggle.
contracts.context: Text alignment, a view switch, zoom: a few choices about one thing. Not for separate actions; those are a .pr-actions row.
relationships: One name for the group: "Text alignment".
Each button keeps its own verb.
accessibility: role="group" with an aria-label.
aria-pressed on toggles.
failures: Never mixes unrelated actions in one group.
Never shows the pressed one by colour alone.
do: Keep it to a few buttons about one thing.
dont: A destructive action inside a group of safe ones.

contracts.name: Card
contracts.layerWhy: It is one item of a collection; the collection, not the card, does a job.
contracts.promise: I am one of several, and you can open me.
contracts.expectation: A raised box among others like it, the whole box a target.
contracts.evidence: It is drawn only inside a list of cards; the title link covers it; its payload stays and wraps while metadata marked data-gives-way goes first.
behaviour: The whole card opens; buttons inside sit above that cover.
Narrower than 15rem, metadata gives way.
contracts.context: Collections people open: reports, issues, products. Never a page, a section, or a lone piece of content.
relationships: Siblings compare; a dynamic list of one is still a list.
accessibility: A list item with a heading link; the ring goes round the card.
failures: Never a single child or a page container.
Never cuts its title.
do: Name its payload; mark what can give way.
dont: A card around a form.

contracts.name: Code block
contracts.layerWhy: It shows code to read and copy; part of a page about code.
contracts.promise: This code can be copied exactly as shown.
contracts.expectation: Code in a well, its language above, Copy Code at the end.
contracts.evidence: Copy Code says "Copied" in place; the code scrolls within itself.
behaviour: The code region is focusable so the keyboard scrolls it.
contracts.context: Documentation, settings that need a snippet.
relationships: Its language names it.
accessibility: A <pre> named by its language.
failures: Never moves the page sideways.
dont: Screenshots of code.

contracts.name: Confirmation
contracts.layerWhy: It asks one question; the action it confirms is its own kind.
contracts.promise: An irreversible action waits for one deliberate yes.
contracts.expectation: A dialog whose answers repeat the action, the safe one first in focus.
contracts.evidence: Resolves true only for its confirm; every way out is false; focus starts on the safe answer for a destructive one.
behaviour: Built on the dialog.
Its confirm is the final danger fill for a destructive action.
contracts.context: Only for what cannot be undone.
relationships: Confirm: "Delete Workspace". Cancel: "Keep Workspace".
accessibility: As the dialog.
failures: Never "OK" or "Yes".
Never for something undoable.
do: Say what is lost in the body.
dont: A confirmation before a save.

inputs: PrimalConfirm.ask({ title, body, confirm, cancel, kind })

contracts.name: Container
contracts.layerWhy: It arranges other parts by space; it keeps no promise to the person of its own.
contracts.promise: Content at a width that reads, or the full width when the product needs it.
contracts.expectation: A centred column with the gutter at its edges.
contracts.evidence: Reading width by default; data-width="full" for app surfaces (decision 11).
behaviour: Centred; the gutter grows with the screen.
contracts.context: The page's main column.
relationships: Every page has one.
accessibility: No semantics of its own.
failures: Never a card around the page.
dont: Nesting containers.

contracts.name: Details
contracts.layerWhy: It lays out facts about one thing; reading facts is not a job.
contracts.promise: Each term is followed by its value.
contracts.expectation: Terms muted, values beside them, stacked on a phone.
contracts.evidence: A real description list; long values wrap.
behaviour: Two columns where there is room, one on a phone.
contracts.context: The facts of one record.
relationships: Terms are short nouns.
accessibility: A native <dl>.
failures: Never a table for one record.
do: Keep terms the same across records.
dont: Details for a list of many things.

contracts.name: Dialog
contracts.layerWhy: It holds a question over the page; the work inside is the cells'.
contracts.promise: Nothing else can happen until this is answered, and there is always a way out.
contracts.expectation: The page covered and still, one box with a title, the answer's buttons, and Close.
contracts.evidence: Close, Escape and the backdrop leave it; focus returns to what opened it; it has no address; on a phone it is a sheet from the bottom.
behaviour: Focus goes to the dialog, so its title is read; Tab stays inside.
Escape closes only the topmost layer.
The page under it does not scroll.
contracts.context: Only a question the work cannot go on without, asked once.
relationships: Its answers sit at the end, the main one last.
A menu or popover may open from it, above it.
accessibility: A native modal <dialog> labelled by its title, described by its description.
failures: Never a dialog for something that can be undone.
Never a dialog with no way out.
Never a place: Back never lands in it.
do: Word its answers as the action.
dont: A dialog for a whole page of work.

contracts.name: Divider
contracts.layerWhy: It arranges other parts by space; it keeps no promise to the person of its own.
contracts.promise: What is before and after are different sections.
contracts.expectation: A thin line where one section ends and the next begins.
contracts.evidence: It is drawn only where that meaning holds; between controls it stands upright.
behaviour: Horizontal in a stack; vertical in a row or toolbar.
contracts.context: Between sections, between groups of controls.
relationships: It separates; space groups.
accessibility: An <hr>, a separator.
failures: Never decoration.
dont: Lines between every row of a form.

contracts.name: Empty state
contracts.layerWhy: It stands where content would be; the next step is someone's action.
contracts.promise: There is nothing here, this is why, and this is what to do.
contracts.expectation: A quiet panel in the content's place with a title, a reason and a button.
contracts.evidence: It names the reason and the next step in place.
behaviour: It is announced as a status.
contracts.context: Empty lists, tables and searches.
relationships: Its button is the next step.
accessibility: role="status".
failures: Never a blank area.
Never a picture instead of words.
dont: "No data."

contracts.name: Field
contracts.layerWhy: It asks one question; answering a whole form is a cell's job.
contracts.promise: One question, with its label, a description when needed, and what's wrong with the answer right under it.
contracts.expectation: A visible label above a control the browser owns, and a message that appears only when there is something to say.
contracts.evidence: After the person has had their go, a wrong answer shows the danger edge and a message under the control that says what to type, in the person's words; optional fields are marked "Optional".
behaviour: The control stays native: autofill, the phone's keyboard and pasting work.
Validates on leaving the field, on input once shown, and on submit.
Messages come from the browser's validity, worded by PRIMAL_MESSAGES; [primalControl]="error" wins.
A search box, a choice, a slider or a colour is never marked Optional.
contracts.context: Wherever the product asks the person something. Not for showing a value that can't change; that is a detail.
relationships: The label is the question; the description says what to give; the message says what to fix.
Inside a group, a radio's message belongs to the group.
accessibility: The label is a <label for>; description and message are linked with aria-describedby.
aria-invalid when wrong; "Error:" read before the message.
The message region is polite, so it is announced as it speaks.
failures: Never an error before the person has had their go.
Never "Invalid input".
Never a placeholder as the label.
do: Mark what is optional, not what is required.
Size the control to the answer.
dont: A field without a visible label.
Errors in a banner far from the field.

contracts.name: Field group
contracts.layerWhy: It asks one question of several controls; still one question, not a whole form.
contracts.promise: These choices answer one question together.
contracts.expectation: A legend over choices close together, and one message for them.
contracts.evidence: A radio group is one tab stop moved by arrows; its message is the group's; as cards, the whole card is the target and the chosen one takes the primary edge.
behaviour: Re-checks every choice when one changes.
With [cards], each choice is a card side by side, wrapping as the width allows.
contracts.context: A set of radios, checkboxes or switches about one thing. Cards when each option needs a few words.
relationships: The legend is the question; each choice's label is an answer.
accessibility: A native <fieldset> and <legend>; arrow keys move within radios as the browser does.
Focus rings the card in card mode.
failures: Never a group without a legend.
Never hides the mark on a card.
do: Use cards for a few options with a sentence each.
dont: Cards for a long list of options.

contracts.name: File drop zone
contracts.layerWhy: One field whose answer is files; part of a form.
contracts.promise: Files can be dropped here or chosen, and the field keeps only the kinds it takes.
contracts.expectation: A big target that takes the primary while a file is over it, and the files listed under it.
contracts.evidence: Each file is listed with its size and Remove; a file the field doesn't accept is left out and named.
behaviour: The native input covers the zone: click, drop and the keyboard all work.
Dropping several when it takes several.
contracts.context: Attachments, imports: when files are the point of the form.
relationships: The description says which kinds and sizes.
accessibility: The native file input is focusable; each Remove is named for its file.
Additions and removals are announced.
failures: Never keeps a file silently that the field can't take.
Never cuts a file name.
do: Say what it takes in the description.
dont: A drop zone for a single profile picture in a long form.

contracts.name: Form
contracts.layerWhy: It holds fields and says when they are all right; the job a form does belongs to the cell around it.
contracts.promise: Pressing its main action either sends a complete answer or shows exactly what is missing.
contracts.expectation: On submit, every wrong field shows its message and focus goes to the first.
contracts.evidence: The browser's bubbles are off; (validSubmit) fires only when every field is valid.
behaviour: novalidate; errors under fields on submit.
Focus moves to the first field that needs attention.
Reset returns every field to untouched.
contracts.context: Any group of fields sent together.
relationships: Its actions sit a section gap under the last field (.pr-form-actions).
accessibility: Focus moves to what needs attention, so a keyboard user lands on it.
failures: Never sends an incomplete answer.
Never clears what was typed on an error.
do: One primary action, worded by what it does.
dont: Validating while the person is still typing their first try.

contracts.name: Grid
contracts.layerWhy: It arranges other parts by space; it keeps no promise to the person of its own.
contracts.promise: Equal columns, as many as fit.
contracts.expectation: Columns that fall to one on a phone.
contracts.evidence: The column count follows the width; --pr-grid-min sets the narrowest.
behaviour: Auto-fill columns at --pr-grid-min.
contracts.context: Metrics, cards, tiles.
relationships: Children are equals.
accessibility: Keeps the markup's order.
failures: Never ranks by column position.
dont: A grid for a form.

contracts.name: Icon button
contracts.layerWhy: A button whose words are its name rather than its face; it keeps the same single-action promise as any button.
contracts.promise: Pressing it does the one thing its name says.
contracts.expectation: A familiar mark (close, edit, more) does what the mark always does.
contracts.evidence: Its name is read aloud and shown on hover (title, or a Primal tooltip); it acknowledges like any button.
behaviour: A square target the height of a control.
Quiet by default: it usually sits among others.
Shows its name as the browser title unless a Primal tooltip is on it.
contracts.context: For actions everyone knows by their mark, on a toolbar, in a corner, at the end of a row. Not for anything that needs its words to be understood.
relationships: It has a name like any button: "Close Panel".
Among icon buttons, the marks share one style and size.
accessibility: aria-label is required: the label input.
The svg is aria-hidden.
At least 24 by 24 pixels.
failures: Never a mark without a name.
Never a mark that means something else elsewhere in the product.
do: Use it for marks with one meaning everywhere.
Give it a tooltip when the mark alone could be read two ways.
dont: An icon button for a rare or unfamiliar action.
Two marks that look alike for different actions.

contracts.name: Inline
contracts.layerWhy: It arranges other parts by space; it keeps no promise to the person of its own.
contracts.promise: Things side by side, wrapping when room runs out.
contracts.expectation: A row aligned on its middles.
contracts.evidence: It wraps instead of overflowing; .pr-push sends one to the end.
behaviour: Wraps; aligns centred.
contracts.context: Name and badge, a row of metadata, a row of buttons.
relationships: .pr-push puts the last thing at the end.
accessibility: Keeps the markup's order.
failures: Never scrolls the page sideways.
dont: Floats.

contracts.name: Link
contracts.layerWhy: It keeps one part of a promise: it takes you somewhere. Moving is never a whole job.
contracts.promise: It takes the person to another place and changes nothing.
contracts.expectation: Following it goes somewhere; it says when that is away from this site or a file.
contracts.evidence: An address on another site opens in a new tab with an arrow shown and "(opens in a new tab)" read; a download shows an arrow down and the file's type and size.
behaviour: External addresses open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer".
A download shows its file type and size when given.
Back always returns to where the person was.
contracts.context: In running text, in lists of places, and as a button-shaped link when it starts a task on its own page.
relationships: Its words name the destination, not "here".
A link that looks like a button still only navigates.
accessibility: A native <a href>.
The new-tab warning is read, not only shown.
The arrows are content with empty alternative text.
failures: Never performs an action.
Never opens a new tab without saying so.
dont: "Click here".
A link that deletes or saves.

inputs: external: opens elsewhere (another site by default)
file: what a download is ("PDF, 2 MB")

contracts.name: List item
contracts.layerWhy: It is one row of a list; the list does the job.
contracts.promise: One thing per row: what it is, a line about it, and its state at the end.
contracts.expectation: Rows divided by thin lines, each with something at the start and the end.
contracts.evidence: The lines mean only "separate items of one list"; the title wraps, never cut.
behaviour: The title links to the thing; the end holds a status or an action.
contracts.context: People, files, reports, results.
relationships: The current item (aria-current) takes the primary's quiet fill.
accessibility: A real <ul> and <li>.
failures: Never repeats a fact (a dot and the same word).
dont: A list item as a page section.

contracts.name: Menu
contracts.layerWhy: It holds commands; each command is an action of its own.
contracts.promise: Pressing the button shows a short list of things to do to one thing.
contracts.expectation: A list beside its button; pressing outside closes it.
contracts.evidence: It opens on the first command, moves with arrows and letters, and returns focus to its button whenever it closes.
behaviour: Enter, Space or ↓ open on the first command; ↑ on the last.
A letter jumps; Home and End go to the ends.
Running a command closes the menu.
Escape closes only the menu.
contracts.context: Actions on one item when there is no room to show them all. Not for navigation between places.
relationships: Its button names what it is about: "Show Report Actions".
A destructive command is in the danger colour, last, after a line.
accessibility: menu and menuitem roles; aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the button.
failures: Never leaves focus in a closed menu.
Never hides the only way to do something essential.
do: Put the destructive command last, apart.
dont: A menu of one command.

contracts.name: Navigation items
contracts.layerWhy: Each item goes to one place; going is not a job.
contracts.promise: This is where each one goes, and the one I am in is marked.
contracts.expectation: A column of place names, the current one in the primary's quiet fill.
contracts.evidence: The current one is marked by fill and aria-current, so it reads without colour too.
behaviour: Each is a link with a real address.
contracts.context: The places of a product or section: a side navigation, settings sections.
relationships: An icon helps find, the word names.
accessibility: Links in a list inside a labelled <nav>.
failures: Never acts; navigation only moves.
do: Keep places where they are, week after week.
dont: An item that opens a dialog.

contracts.name: Number
contracts.layerWhy: One field whose answer is a number; part of a form.
contracts.promise: A number typed or stepped, never past its limits.
contracts.expectation: The value between − and +, its unit beside it.
contracts.evidence: − and + stop at min and max (disabled there), repeat while held, and keep focus in the input.
behaviour: Steps by the field's step; an empty field starts from its min.
Arrow keys and typing work as in any number field.
contracts.context: Counts, quantities, percentages, weights.

failures: Never steps past a limit.
dont: A stepper for a phone number or a year.

contracts.name: Pagination
contracts.layerWhy: It moves through one list; moving is never a job.
contracts.promise: Each page of the same list is one press away, and this one is marked.
contracts.expectation: Previous, the pages near yours, the first and last, and Next.
contracts.evidence: The current page is in the primary's quiet fill and announced as current; the row keeps its length.

dont: Pagination for ten items.

contracts.name: Popover
contracts.layerWhy: It holds a little beside the page; the page stays the person's own.
contracts.promise: A few details or a small task beside its button, gone when you press outside.
contracts.expectation: A raised box against its button.
contracts.evidence: Focus moves into it if it holds something to press, and returns to the button on close.
behaviour: Opens and closes from its button; Escape and a press outside close it.
Placed against its button, flipped when there is no room, in either direction.
contracts.context: Small details or a small form about one thing.
relationships: Its button says what it holds.
accessibility: role="dialog" with a label; aria-haspopup and aria-expanded on the button.
failures: Never blocks the page.
Never drops focus to the top of the page.
dont: A popover for a long form.

contracts.name: Progress
contracts.layerWhy: It shows how far one job has gone; the job is someone else's.
contracts.promise: The work has a known length and this is how far along it is.
contracts.expectation: A bar with words and a percentage.
contracts.evidence: Its value is real; without one it travels as clearly not a number.
behaviour: Shows the percentage when there is a value.
Without a value, a band travels the track.
contracts.context: Uploads, imports, exports: measurable work.
relationships: Its label names the work: "Uploading 12 photos".
accessibility: A native <progress> named by its label.
failures: Never faked.
do: Give it a value as soon as you know one.
dont: A progress bar that loops forever on known work.

contracts.name: Row of actions
contracts.layerWhy: It places actions by their weight; it decides no job of its own.
contracts.promise: Safe actions sit together at the end, the main one last; a destructive one sits apart.
contracts.expectation: The main action is where the hand expects it, and taking something away is never next to keeping it.
contracts.evidence: The destructive action is a section gap from the safe ones and in the danger treatment; on a phone the row stacks.
behaviour: Danger at the start, safe group at the end.
Wraps on narrow widths with the main action first in reading.
contracts.context: At the end of a form, a dialog or a detail.
relationships: It holds buttons; their emphasis ranks them.
The distance is the decision on destructive actions (0.5.0).
accessibility: Order in the markup is the reading and tab order.
failures: Never puts Delete between Cancel and Save.
do: One primary at the end of the group.
dont: Two destructive actions in one row.

contracts.name: Scroll area
contracts.layerWhy: It arranges other parts by space; it keeps no promise to the person of its own.
contracts.promise: A region that scrolls within itself and never moves the page.
contracts.expectation: A box with its own scroll.
contracts.evidence: It is focusable and named, so the keyboard scrolls it too.
behaviour: --pr-scroll-height sets its height.
Overscroll is contained.
contracts.context: Long activity, logs, lists inside a panel.
relationships: It belongs to the section around it.
accessibility: tabindex="0", role="region" and a label.
failures: Never traps the page's scroll.
dont: Scroll areas inside scroll areas.

contracts.name: Search field
contracts.layerWhy: It is one field: a way in, not a question.
contracts.promise: Typing here finds things.
contracts.expectation: A field with a magnifier at its start.
contracts.evidence: The magnifier says what it is before a word is read; it is never marked Optional.
behaviour: The native search input keeps Escape to clear.
contracts.context: Bars, lists, the top of results.
relationships: Its placeholder may say what it searches, its label must.
accessibility: A labelled <input type="search">, inside a search landmark where it searches the page.
failures: Never without a label.
dont: A search field that filters by default without saying so.

contracts.name: Select
contracts.layerWhy: It is one field whose answer is one option; a primitive part of a form.
contracts.promise: One answer from a known list, chosen by pointing or by the keyboard.
contracts.expectation: A field with a chevron that opens a list Primal draws, the chosen option checked.
contracts.evidence: The list sits against the field, the active option is shaded and the chosen one checked; the native select keeps the value for forms and autofill.
behaviour: Opens on click, Enter, Space or ↓; arrows move; typing jumps; Escape closes.
Groups have headings.
contracts.context: Five or more options. Fewer: radios.
relationships: Its label is the question; the options are answers.
accessibility: combobox and listbox roles; aria-activedescendant follows the active option.
failures: Never hides the chosen value.
Never loses the native value.
do: Put the most common answer where the eye lands.
dont: A select for yes or no.

contracts.name: Shaped input
contracts.layerWhy: It shapes one answer as it is typed; it is part of a field.
contracts.promise: The answer arrives in the form it is asked for, without fighting the person.
contracts.expectation: Separators appear as they type; pasting is shaped too.
contracts.evidence: The caret stays where they type; deleting runs back cleanly; email, phone and website have ready shapes.
behaviour: phone: a pattern of digits (000-000-0000), a leading + kept as typed.
email: no spaces, one @, the domain in lower case.
url: https:// written in on focus, cleared if left alone.
Any pattern: 0 digit, a letter, * either.
contracts.context: Phone numbers, emails, websites, codes with a known shape.
relationships: It sits on a field's native input.
accessibility: Sets inputmode so the phone shows the right keyboard.
failures: Never moves the caret away.
Never refuses a paste.
do: Use the pattern your country uses.
dont: A mask that blocks a valid international number.

inputs: primalMask: phone | email | url | a pattern

contracts.name: Skeleton
contracts.layerWhy: It holds the shape of content that is coming; the content is someone else's.
contracts.promise: This is where content will be, and this is its shape.
contracts.expectation: Blocks the size and shape of the rows, text and pictures to come.
contracts.evidence: It sits inside a container marked aria-busy, and is hidden from assistive technology.
behaviour: Shimmers slowly; still under reduced motion.
contracts.context: Lists and pages whose shape is known before their data.
relationships: It mirrors the real row: an avatar and two lines become a circle and two lines.
accessibility: aria-hidden; the container's aria-busy is what is heard.
failures: Never a shape that doesn't match what arrives.
dont: A skeleton when the data is already there.

contracts.name: Spinner
contracts.layerWhy: It says one thing, "working", and nothing about when it ends.
contracts.promise: Something is happening and its length is unknown.
contracts.expectation: A turning mark beside the work.
contracts.evidence: It is used only when neither the shape nor the length of what is coming is known, and it is read as its label.
behaviour: Turns steadily; under reduced motion it breathes instead.
contracts.context: Short waits of unknown length. A list that is loading uses skeletons; measurable work uses progress.
relationships: Its label says what is happening: "Checking the address".
accessibility: role="status" with a visually hidden label.
failures: Never hides a known shape or length.
dont: A spinner for a page whose layout is known.

contracts.name: Stack
contracts.layerWhy: It arranges other parts by space; it keeps no promise to the person of its own.
contracts.promise: Things one under the other, a known gap apart.
contracts.expectation: Grouping by space alone.
contracts.evidence: Strip every border and fill and the grouping still reads.
behaviour: data-gap: component, group (default) or section.
A list as a stack drops its bullets.
contracts.context: Any group read top to bottom: a profile, a form's fields, a list of facts.
relationships: The gap says how related the parts are.
accessibility: Keeps the markup's order.
failures: Never a box to make a group.
dont: Margins on each child instead.

contracts.name: Status
contracts.layerWhy: It says how one thing stands; no job.
contracts.promise: This is fine, needs attention, has stopped, hasn't started, or is under way.
contracts.expectation: A mark and a word at the end of a row, saying how that row stands.
contracts.evidence: The mark's shape says the state (dot, triangle, square, ring, half), the word says it fully, the colour only adds.
behaviour: Five states, each with its own shape.
contracts.context: Records with a state: invoices, members, jobs.
relationships: One status per item.
accessibility: The word is the accessible text; the mark is decoration.
failures: Never colour alone.
dont: A status dot with no word.

contracts.name: Table
contracts.layerWhy: It shows rows to read across and down; what a table is about is the page's job.
contracts.promise: Rows of the same kind, read across and down, sortable by any column.
contracts.expectation: Column headers that sort, numbers lined up, and an empty table that says why.
contracts.evidence: Each header sorts ascending, descending, then back; it shows which way and announces it; numbers and dates sort by value.
behaviour: On by default; [sortable]="false" for a table, data-sort="false" for a column.
data-sort-value and <time datetime> sort by value.
With (sorted) bound, the data is sorted by you, not the rows.
contracts.context: Data people compare. Not for layout.
relationships: A .pr-table wrapper scrolls it within itself.
accessibility: Headers are buttons inside <th> with aria-sort.
The scroll wrapper is a focusable, named region.
failures: Never moves the page sideways.
Never sorts a table whose order is its meaning.
dont: A table for a form layout.

contracts.name: Tabs
contracts.layerWhy: It switches between faces of one thing; it moves, and does no job of its own.
contracts.promise: Each tab is another face of the same thing, and choosing one shows it at once.
contracts.expectation: A row of names with the chosen one underlined, and its face under it.
contracts.evidence: The chosen tab is underlined in the primary and announced as selected; faces keep their state while hidden.
behaviour: One tab stop; ← → move and show (following the reading direction); Home and End go to the ends.
Disabled tabs are skipped.
contracts.context: Summary, Data, History of one report. Never unrelated places, never filters.
relationships: Each tab labels its panel; a tab worth sharing keeps its face in the address.
accessibility: tablist, tab and tabpanel roles, linked by ids.
Panels are focusable.
failures: Never a filter.
Never loses what was typed in a hidden face.
do: Put the most used face first.
dont: Tabs that navigate between unrelated pages.

contracts.name: Toast
contracts.layerWhy: It reports one outcome where the person can no longer see it; it is a voice of other parts, not a job.
contracts.promise: Something just happened out of sight, and it can be undone for a moment.
contracts.expectation: A short message in the corner that fades, with Undo when there is one.
contracts.evidence: It stays five seconds, eight with an action, waits while pointed at or focused, and announces itself politely.
behaviour: At most three; a newer one pushes the oldest out.
Escape closes the newest.
Its action closes it after running.
It sits above dialogs (a manual popover).
contracts.context: The outcome of an action whose place is gone, or of work that finished elsewhere. Never routine outcomes, lasting facts, questions or errors to fix.
relationships: Its place is "toast" in the behaviour model.
It holds the undo of a reversible destructive action.
accessibility: A labelled region with a polite live region.
Its buttons are real buttons in the tab order.
failures: Never the only place an error shows.
Never takes an undo away while it is being read.
dont: "Success!"
A toast for a saved setting.

contracts.name: Toolbar
contracts.layerWhy: It groups controls for one thing; each control is its own action.
contracts.promise: The controls for this thing, one tab stop.
contracts.expectation: A row of controls under a line, groups divided.
contracts.evidence: Tab reaches it once; arrows move between controls, following the reading direction; the last used is remembered.
behaviour: Home and End go to the ends.
Text fields keep their arrows.
contracts.context: Editors, tables, documents.
relationships: Groups split by .pr-divider.
accessibility: role="toolbar" with a label; a roving tab stop.
failures: Never more than one tab stop.
dont: A toolbar of unrelated actions.

contracts.name: Tooltip
contracts.layerWhy: It is a phrase about one thing; it does nothing.
contracts.promise: A short description of what I am pointing at or focused on.
contracts.expectation: A dark label above the thing after a moment.
contracts.evidence: It shows on hover after half a second and at once on keyboard focus, hides on leaving and Escape, and is read as the thing's description.
behaviour: Never interactive.
Hidden on press.
contracts.context: What an icon means; a shortcut.
relationships: It adds to the thing's name; it never replaces it.
accessibility: role="tooltip" linked by aria-describedby.
failures: Never holds the only copy of something important (no hover on a phone).
dont: A link inside a tooltip.

contracts.name: Item tile
contracts.layerWhy: It shows one item with its payload named and kept, a whole job of presenting a thing in a collection.
contracts.promise: The one thing this tile exists to show stays, whatever the width.
contracts.expectation: A card with its state, its title, and metadata that gives way.
contracts.evidence: At 320px with real-length data the title is shown in full; in a narrow tile the number, labels and assignee give way first.
behaviour: Payload: the title.
Built on the card.
contracts.context: Issues, tasks, products in a board or grid.
relationships: A status, badges and an avatar around the payload.
accessibility: As the card.
failures: Never cuts the payload while metadata survives.
do: Mark everything but the payload data-gives-way.
dont: Truncating the title with an ellipsis.

contracts.name: Search with results
contracts.layerWhy: It does one whole job, finding things, with every result and feedback state, from primitives only.
contracts.promise: Type, and see what matches, how many, and what to do when nothing does.
contracts.expectation: A search field and its results under it.
contracts.evidence: Waiting shows the results' shape; then a count and each result with the match marked; none offers a way out; a failure offers Try Again.
behaviour: Payload: the results.
Waits 250 ms after typing; a late answer never replaces a newer one.
Empty shows its blank list (popular).
Escape clears.
contracts.context: Docs, records, a product's whole content.
relationships: Built from a search field, list items, skeletons, an empty state and an alert.
accessibility: A search landmark; the count and states are announced.
failures: Never a blank result area.
dont: A search that only works on Enter with no feedback.

contracts.name: Subscribe
contracts.layerWhy: It does one whole job, subscribing someone, end to end with its feedback, from primitives only.
contracts.promise: Give an email and get what was promised, or be told exactly what to fix.
contracts.expectation: A promise, an email field and one button.
contracts.evidence: It ends in a subscription said in place, naming the address, or in an error under the field that says what to do; nothing is left to the page.
behaviour: Payload: the promise.
Busy at once; a bad address or a failure keeps what was typed.
"Use Another Address" starts over.
contracts.context: A newsletter, release notes, a waitlist.
relationships: Built from a field, a shaped input, a button and an alert.
accessibility: The result is announced; focus returns to the field on an error.
failures: Never ends without saying what happened.
Never loses the typed address.
do: Say what arrives and how often.
dont: A subscribe form that only says "Thanks!"

contracts.name: App shell
contracts.layerWhy: It is the place every other place sits in: a whole layout of the product's journey between places.
contracts.promise: The bar and the navigation hold still; the place changes.
contracts.expectation: A bar across the top, places at the side, the place itself.
contracts.evidence: Narrow, the navigation and search fold behind Show Menu, nothing lost; choosing a place closes the menu.
behaviour: Lays itself out by its own width.
The current place is marked in the navigation.
contracts.context: Every product with more than one place.
relationships: Next two moves: the other places at the side, the account in the bar.
accessibility: Landmarks: navigation and main, each named.
failures: Never moves the navigation between visits.
do: Keep places in the same order forever.
dont: Hiding search on a phone with no way to it.

contracts.name: Authentication
contracts.layerWhy: It is a place where several cells (sign-in, sign-up, reset) serve one journey: getting in.
contracts.promise: Get in, get an account, or get back in when the password is lost, each at its own address.
contracts.expectation: A narrow column with the product's name, one question at a time, no card.
contracts.evidence: Each place restores from a cold link; a mismatch says so beside the form with the reset; every place links to the other two.
behaviour: Sign-in, sign-up and reset at /sign-in, /sign-up, /reset.
The email typed at sign-in carries to the reset.
The reset never says whether an account exists.
contracts.context: The way into any product.
relationships: Next two moves: switch between sign-in and sign-up, and reach the reset.
accessibility: Autocomplete hints for password managers; errors under fields.
failures: Never a dead end.
Never a card around the form.
do: Carry what was typed between places.
dont: A sign-in in a modal over the product.

contracts.name: List and detail
contracts.layerWhy: It is a place where the list, the detail and their actions serve the journey of managing things.
contracts.promise: Find a thing, open it, change it, delete it, or make one; each at its own address.
contracts.expectation: The list beside the open item, or each on its own with a way back.
contracts.evidence: Every item opens cold from its readable address; delete has Undo; a new thing opens; the list keeps its state while items open.
behaviour: /list-detail/<slug>, never a bare id.
Narrow, the list or the item shows, with "All reports".
Delete apart from Rename.
contracts.context: Records: reports, customers, invoices.
relationships: Next two moves: rename and delete beside the title; New Report above the list.
accessibility: The open item is marked in the list; changes are announced.
failures: Never stops at create: edit and delete are there.
dont: Ids in the address.

contracts.name: Multi-step form
contracts.layerWhy: It is a place where several forms serve one long journey, step by step.
contracts.promise: I can see the steps, go back without losing anything, and check everything before it's done.
contracts.expectation: Numbered steps, the current one in the primary, a review with Change.
contracts.evidence: The step is in the address; Back goes to the step before; a step that can't be shown yet sends the address back to the first.
behaviour: Answers kept across steps.
Done steps are checked and revisitable.
The last step is a review.
contracts.context: Onboarding, checkout, setup.
relationships: Next two moves: Back, and the step after.
accessibility: Steps in an ordered list with aria-current="step".
failures: Never loses an answer.
Never jumps ahead of what is answered.
dont: More steps than the task needs.

contracts.name: Settings
contracts.layerWhy: It is a place: sections of settings, each a cell, serving the journey of changing how the product works.
contracts.promise: Each section has its own address; changes are saved as they are made.
contracts.expectation: Sections at the side, the section's settings beside them.
contracts.evidence: A switch says "Saved" beside itself; a form says it on its button; the irreversible sits apart behind a confirmation.
behaviour: /settings/<section> restores cold.
On a phone the sections sit above as a row.
contracts.context: Every product's settings.
relationships: Next two moves: the other sections, Save Changes at the end of a form.
accessibility: The current section is marked aria-current.
failures: Never loses a change on leaving.
dont: One giant Save for every section.
